lines.text: under disgrace, salvation under ruin, ascendancy under
exile, heaven under hell, wisdom under folly, righteousness
under sin, power under weakness; and in general every
assurance of the good under the refusal of just that good we
desire, so that sheer faith in God may come first" (II, 219,
16ff.). "Whoever is wise, accepts God's gifts with patience
and joy; but the highest insight is needed if our wisdom is not
to focus itself on what lies exposed to our view (in that case
we should have to despair), but on what is future, unknown
and not exposed to our gaze" (II, 206, 27ff.). Hence this is
the choice and decision which lie before us. But whoever
can say: "The Lord is my portion", can also continue: "The
Lord is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul that
seeks Him" (3: 25).
Oh that we might succeed at one stroke in deciding aright
this either-or! Then at one stroke the burden of our anxieties
would drop from us. Free and unencumbered could we
traverse our trials and distresses, inwardly freed from self-
will, and no evil could any longer affect us in our inmost
self. There may well be people who succeed in doing so, who
in a childlike spirit of confidence pass calmly through all
terrors, as in the fairy story the lucky child passes cheerful
and unharmed among roaming wild beasts which can do
him no hurt, because he is magically protected.
But how few there are whose childlike faith as a magic
armour protects them from all the assaults of the devil, from
doubt and bitter anxiety and fear! We others, who are by
far the greater number-must we not ever strive with might
and main to secure this magic armour and to appropriate
this faith? Must we not repeatedly renew the decision, and
win an ever new victory over ourselves as we determine that
the Lord shall be our portion? To us is addressed with special
force the verse: "It is good that one should wait quietly
for the salvation of the Lord" (3: 26). "Wait quietly"-
that is what we must learn to do. Such patience implies that
we shall ever renew our decision, confess our faith in the
Lord, turn away from ourselves and from the world, and
hope in "the salvation of the Lord".
